response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if some laboratory record has U-PRO = '-' and some record has RA = '-'; both are in the same record (the same row), not necessarily across different records.
TAT - TAT2 is computed per row, so rows where either is NULL are ignored; patients with no non-null values are excluded from the final averages.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient qualifies if some record has U-PRO = '-' and (possibly a different) record has RA = '-'.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(`U-PRO` = '-') > 0 AND SUM(RA = '-') > 0), per AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per
